correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the quantified theorem for every measurable nonzero non-increasing W with all moments finite and every entire f,g in F_W^2. After normalizing m0=1, write s=m1>0 and T with density W. The 2026 source Proposition 6.1/Lemma 6.3 proves that nu=Law(max(T,s)) satisfies the sharp moment inequalities. For coefficient differences d_k=|a_k|^2-|b_k|^2 set x_k=(d_k)_+,y_k=(-d_k)_+ and entire X(t),Y(t). The exact source inequality X(t)<=s Y(t)/t for t>=s and source moment-duality chain sandwich sum x_k m_k and sum y_k m_k. Equality of norms makes every link equality. Because the nondegenerate T has mean s below its essential supremum and W is non-increasing, nu has positive density on some interval (s,b); thus the nonnegative middle defect sY(t)-tX(t) vanishes there and identically by the identity theorem. For every r>sqrt(s), equality in the two-sided circle estimate gives equality in the pointwise Schwarz-Pick inequality wherever g!=0, so f/g is a disk automorphism under inversion and equals (a z+eta sqrt(s))/(z+conj(a) eta sqrt(s)), |a|<1. Entire cancellation gives f=(a z+eta sqrt(s))h, g=(z+conj(a) eta sqrt(s))h; h,zh are norm-finite since they are linear combinations of f,g. Direct radial coefficient expansion yields ||g||^2-||f||^2=(1-|a|^2)sum_j |h_j|^2 (m_{j+1}-s m_j). The j=0 term vanishes and j>=1 terms are strictly positive Cov(T,T^j) by 1/2 E[(T-T')(T^j-T'^j)]>0. Therefore h is constant. Conversely the explicit linear family obeys |g|^2-|f|^2=|c|^2(1-|a|^2)(|z|^2-s) and equal norms because m1=s*m0. The unimodular case, zero pair, compactly supported monotone weights, boundary equality and arbitrary all-moment non-smooth monotone W are covered. The proof is analytic and uses no finite-experiment extrapolation.
risks: Relies on the verified published sharp-radius/moment-duality theorem and its Schwarz-Pick estimate rather than reproving all of those published lemmas from first principles; the formulas and hypotheses were checked against the full primary proof.
F_W^2 can be noncomplete for compactly supported W, but h and zh are explicit linear combinations of the given norm-finite entire f,g, so all coefficient sums used are finite.

evidence: Wikström Theorem 1.1 is the special Gaussian weight; Theorem 1.3 is sharp radius/admissibility for monotone weights; Remark 5.3 notes the Gaussian equality argument only used support of a moment measure. Section 7 Proposition 7.1 states any boundary-tight finite-Blaschke quotient has linear equality.

For every nondegenerate monotone density W, nu=Law(max(T,s)) has positive density on a nonempty open interval just above mean s, though not necessarily full support up to infinity (compactly supported W). Equality in the integrated coefficient defect therefore forces tX=sY on an interval, whence everywhere by analyticity. This supplies equality in Schwarz-Pick and excludes non-boundary-tight extremizers.
For the Möbius quotient the norm defect equals (1-|a|^2) sum_j |h_j|^2 (m_{j+1}-s*m_j), and m_{j+1}-s*m_j=Cov(T,T^j)>0 for j>=1; this rules out nonlinear multipliers for each nondegenerate weight.
The broad published radius result proves no rigidity and explicitly excludes equality classification from its scope.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Radius admissibility plus the existence of linear sharp pairs does not logically state uniqueness. The Gaussian rigidity argument in the source is extremely close; transferring it to compactly supported or irregular monotone weights requires verifying positive density on an interval suffices in place of full half-line support, and then strict moment covariance. These steps yield the claimed all-weight result. Because the method is close to the source, priority is qualified and the contribution is limited to complete rigidity, not radius sharpness.

value.rationale: At the known sharp Korenblum radius, classifying *every* norm-equality pair is the natural exact extremal problem for weighted Fock Hilbert spaces. The theorem gives a complete and weight-independent normalized rigidity law throughout an infinite family including stretched exponentials and compactly supported monotone weights, ruling out all nonlinear extremizers even when the moment certificate has only interval, not half-line, support. It is stronger than furnishing one probe pair or the radius value and can inform stability and perturbation work. Value credit is solely for this exact rigidity, not for the already-published sharp radius or Gaussian special case.
risks: The mathematical contribution is tightly connected to the published moment-duality proof and does not give quantitative near-equality stability or general p norms.
